clinical_knowledge.topic: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) evaluation and management
core_concepts: GAD is excessive, difficult-to-control worry across several domains for at least 6 months with associated symptoms and impairment.
Assess impairment, panic, depression, mania, substance use, medicines, trauma, and medical contributors such as thyroid disease when indicated.
CBT and other structured psychological therapies are first-line options; discuss medication only after individualized assessment and shared decision-making.
Benzodiazepines are not routine long-term treatment because of dependence, sedation, and withdrawal risks.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Adjustment disorder without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Acute suicidal or homicidal ideation.
management_principles: Assess safety, severity, functional impairment, and medical or substance-related causes; a GAD-7 can support but not replace clinical assessment.
Offer CBT and discuss SSRI or SNRI treatment when appropriate, including adverse effects, interactions, early activation, and follow-up.
Urgently assess and escalate for suicidal intent, psychosis, mania, severe self-neglect, or inability to remain safe.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.
